No. As @sqeak mentioned, the strings are just models for fundamental particles. It isn't even that the particles need to be strings, it's just that the same mathematics applies, so it's an easy way to conceptualize them.

I've seen an analogy for spooky action at a distance (entanglement/nonlocality) that talks about the entangled particles being linked by a string, so possibly this is where the confusion arises.

Also, is everything connected with everything

From a QM perspective, yes (nothing to do with string theory afaik). Particles have a wave-like nature. This can be interpreted probabilistically: the location of the particle is undetermined and it has a certain probability of being in any given location at a given time. However, QM experiments (double slit, etc.) show us that it's a bit more complicated that this - the particle is in all of those places at any given time (it is in a superstate of all possible positions) until it is observed. The thing is, the wave function of a particle extends across all of spacetime; consequently, there is an overlap of the wavefunction of your coffee cup with the sun, and the potential for interaction.

String Theory is simply a model of all fundamental particles. It puts forth that the so-called point particles, like the electron, are actually much smaller vibrating strands (or strings) of energy. In fact, most strings in String Theory are closed loops, like a rubberband. Nothing in String Theory puts forth that things are connected any more than they already are by the infinite reach of gravitational or electromagnetic force.
